types.definition: An expressed title, name or particular identifying reference to a book or audiobook. Require the work role and particular-reference relation in the utterance; generic content selection alone does not count. Apply expressed-communicative-content scope.

Require both an expressed reference to a particular work/collection and evidence of the requested work type. A title/name can supply identity, but a proper title or resolved database identifier is not required.

Anaphoric, possessive, ordinal or history-relative expressions such as that song, my audiobook, track eight or the last song can supply a particular reference when the work role is expressed. Do not resolve which work it denotes from missing history.

A request for arbitrary content satisfying a genre, topic, quality or provider criterion does not by itself identify a particular work. Some folk songs or a new podcast on healthcare is selection, not a work reference. A superlative alone is not proof of an already identified work.

Determine whether a description refers to an established/specific work or merely restricts an open search. Definite or possessive determiners are evidence, not automatic lexical rules. If the distinction is not supported by the full utterance, keep unavailable.

Explicit naming, called/named constructions, creator-work relations with a supplied work label, work nouns and continuation references can establish type and identity. Play plus an ambiguous name alone does not decide song versus artist, album, film or another type.
A provider, creator or medium alone does not imply an identified work. If creator/provider wording leaves one particular work versus unspecified content unresolved, keep unavailable.

Game names include conventionally named rule systems such as chess and rock paper scissors when used as games; an open game genre or an ambiguous sport-versus-digital-game request does not automatically identify a game work.

An identified playlist can be specified by its name, ordinal, owner or identifying description. An arbitrary newly requested playlist defined only by selection criteria is not an established work reference unless an explicit identifying label/reference is assigned.

Presence is independent of intent, playback commitment and value recovery. A negated or excluded identified work can still be content-relevant. Each other type requires its own evidence; do not propagate a work type from native labels or external title facts.
types.negative_supervision_policy: Full-input review establishes only generic content/category/provider selection or no reference of this type; native omission is not absence.

Separate the assistant operation from the event content it operates on. Turn off the lights alone does not express an additional event argument; remind me to turn off the lights does, because turning off is the reminder content.

Accept event nouns, descriptive labels and clauses representing activities or occurrences. A proper event name, concrete participant identity, exact time, or normalized executable value is not required.

Generic object properties, static personal attributes and content-category words alone are not events.

An event in requested message content or task-list content counts independently of the native intent. A bare request to send, play, search, switch or schedule without separately expressed event content does not gain event presence merely from that operation verb.

Explicitly stated events count as communicated content, including independent reports and descriptive clauses. Do not infer an event from a bare assistant operation or from external background absent from the input.

Determine whether a description refers to an established/specific work or merely restricts an open search. Definite or possessive determiners are evidence, not automatic lexical rules. If the distinction is not supported by the full utterance, keep unavailable.

A provider, creator or medium alone does not imply an identified work. If creator/provider wording leaves one particular work versus unspecified content unresolved, keep unavailable.

Game names include conventionally named rule systems such as chess and rock paper scissors when used as games; an open game genre or an ambiguous sport-versus-digital-game request does not automatically identify a game work.

An identified playlist can be specified by its name, ordinal, owner or identifying description. An arbitrary newly requested playlist defined only by selection criteria is not an established work reference unless an explicit identifying label/reference is assigned.

role_rules.rule: Count an explicitly expressed property/role when its type is established, including an interrogative asking for its value. Do not require the answer value to occur in the input. Never infer a role solely because the task usually needs that parameter; generic domain words alone are not all of its properties.
role_rules.boundary: Count an expressed meteorological condition/property or an explicitly supported weather-protection criterion, including a question asking for temperature, humidity, rainfall or another identified weather property without its answer value. Generic weather/forecast/climate words alone do not specify a condition/property. Temperature in a cooking, body or device context is not automatically meteorological; ambiguous domain evidence remains unavailable. A practical clothing/equipment question counts when the utterance establishes a weather-related need, for example rain protection or warmth outside. Sandals, pants, hats, jackets, windows or swimming alone can have non-weather purposes; do not use native weather intent to settle that ambiguity. Do not require a positive forecast or committed action: asking whether it will rain expresses rain even if the answer may be no. The task detects the expressed property, not actual weather.

role_rules.rule: An explicitly expressed meteorological condition, property or supported weather-protection criterion, including a question asking for a particular weather property. A generic weather request alone is insufficient. Apply expressed-communicative-content scope. Solar/lunar geometry, astronomical event timing and daylight duration alone are outside this meteorological predicate.
role_rules.boundary: Sunrise/sunset timing, solar/lunar distance or mass, moon phase and daylight duration are astronomical/temporal properties, not weather descriptors by themselves. Time/date/event predicates must be assessed independently. Sunny/sunshine as an outdoor condition or forecast does express a meteorological property. A song title containing sunshine does not. Temperature at sunset explicitly adds a meteorological property; sunset alone does not. Clothing/protection objects and windows are not automatically weather evidence. Sun glasses without a supported exposure/weather criterion remains ambiguous; do not settle it from native weather labels. Existing explicit weather-protection policy remains applicable.

role_rules.rule: Assess roles expressed anywhere in the supplied utterance content: requests, questions, standalone or coordinated assertions/preferences, constraints, descriptions, reasons, and quoted/requested payloads. Do not exclude an expressed clause merely because it is unrelated to another requested operation. Conversational framing alone supplies no task role; per-type evidence and presence policies still apply. Scope inclusion does not infer an action, answer, commitment or external state.
role_rules.boundary: Mixed clauses receive the same scope whether linked by and, but or an explicit reason, or independently stated. Do not infer an invisible primary-request/background split. This deliberately supersedes v1 unrelated-background exclusion; it is a project convention, not user-confirmed preference or official SLURP annotation. Scope and type identifiability are separate. I like it is in scope although it may not identify music, a song or another type. Unknown referent/type remains unavailable for affected predicates; the statement is not out of scope. Bare fragments are in scope as supplied content. A fragment such as tennis can establish a sport without inventing a search or playback request; pop may remain ambiguous between genre/sound/other senses. Definition_word still requires an explicit meaning/definition target, not every bare noun. A word used only as a title, spelling/definition target or string is not automatically a referent of its ordinary type. A requested quoted sentence can express roles in its represented scene; do not treat the sentence as an instruction to execute. Negation, denial, hypotheticals and correction preserve expressed roles; slot presence does not decide which value is accepted or which state is true. Native intent and entity omission cannot supply missing evidence. Reported events and their participants can count; the bare assistant operation still does not create event_name. I in I went to the park is a reported participant; I want/please tell me/assistant address alone is conversational framing. Content-scope changes only S predicates. Do not automatically change native Final, classify a mentioned intention as I_present, or infer intent-slot binding from role cooccurrence. The scope is task-level input shared across queries. No gold-based question selection or sample-topic routing; original metadata/transcripts remain offline review evidence, never actor input.

types.historical_boundary_review: Examples include clothing/equipment terms; literal-weather-only definitions would miss the release convention.
types.boundary_review: Apply explicit contextual-role rules; distinguish proven absence from genuinely ambiguous domain or attachment. No native-label or world-knowledge closure.

overlap_rule: For each configured type, require its own expressed-role evidence, presence policy and scope. The same expression may support multiple true predicates when each definition is satisfied and no explicit task rule excludes that overlap.
no_automatic_closure: A type hierarchy, shared word, native positive or external real-world identity does not automatically establish another predicate.
